hints.junior: Initial render got dramatically faster, then someone scrolled down and the scrollbar started visibly jumping around — worse than before.
hints.mid: content-visibility: auto skips layout and paint for irrelevant sections, but doesn't reserve any space for what it's skipping.
hints.staff: Not a bug — auto applies size containment as part of skipping render, and size containment means computing size without looking at contents at all.

hints.junior: Each section really does carry content-visibility auto — click Auto-scroll and watch the layout-jumps counter react.
hints.mid: Broken has no contain-intrinsic-size, so unrendered sections collapse and the container height snaps around as you pass them.
hints.staff: Try DevTools' Rendering panel with Layout Shift Regions enabled while scrolling broken mode — the highlights fire on every section boundary.

hints.junior: contain-intrinsic-size gives the browser a placeholder height to use while a section is skipped, so total page height stays roughly correct.
hints.mid: Use the auto keyword form — the fallback covers the first render, then the browser remembers the real measured height after that.
hints.staff: The fallback doesn't need to be exact, just close enough to keep the placeholder-to-real shift under your CLS budget — size it per section type, not one constant.

hints.junior: Apply content-visibility to individual sections, not one wrapper around the whole page — a single wrapper just moves the all-or-nothing cost around.
hints.mid: Find-in-page and #fragment links both work correctly through skipped content — the browser temporarily renders a matched section, no workaround needed.
hints.staff: Test sticky or fixed descendants explicitly — size containment on the ancestor can affect how their containing block resolves, breaking sticky positioning.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about a long page that got faster with one CSS property, then started visibly jumping around the moment someone scrolled it.
The fix is a second property, contain intrinsic size, set right alongside it. It tells the browser roughly how tall a skipped section is, so the page doesn't keep resizing itself as you scroll.
Auto-scroll through the same eight sections in both modes and watch the layout jump counter react to the same behavior the spec describes.
Content visibility auto skips rendering to save time, but it needs a size hint or the page will jump around as you scroll. Always pair the two.
